newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: SKI JUMPING-PETERKA SEALS SKI FLYING TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-PETERKA SEALS SKI FLYING TITLE.

text.p: One day after becoming the first Slovenian to seal victory in the ski jumping World Cup, teenager Primoz Peterka claimed the ski flying title with a second place in the season's final event on Sunday.
Peterka, 18 and only in his second winter on the World Cup tour, kept his nerve in front of a roaring home crowd of 65,000 to improve on a first leg ninth place with jumps of 186 and 195 metres.
His only rival in the fight for the flying trophy and winner of Saturday's first of two back-to-back events in Planica, Japan's Takanobu Okabe, failed to qualify for the second leg on Sunday.
"I am delighted to have won the ski flying title. But I am even happier that I managed such a good second jump in front of my people," said Peterka, who has 290 ski flying points to Okabe's 260.
"It is a great feeling to have won both titles at home. Now I have to get some sleep in order to have the power to celebrate," he added. "A big stone has fallen from my heart now."
The Slovenian economics student from the town of Moravce said his goal for next season was to win a medal at the Nagano Olympics.
"I have never participated in Olympics. Nagano is my main aim although I do not really like big events," said Peterka, who left the season's world championships in Trondheim empty handed.
Peterka had a bad start to the ski jumping finals on the biggest competition hill in world, when he fell heavily during training on Friday and sustained bruising to the head and back.
However, on Saturday, Peterka pulled himself together and finished fourth to clinch the overall title from his only remaining rival Germany's Dieter Thoma, who finished behind him in sixth place.

It was an overall disappointing weekend for Thoma who on Sunday lost a first leg lead -- in which he posted the day's longest jump of 211 metres -- after a poor second jump of only 109 metres to fall back to 14th place.
Peterka completed the season with 1,402 points ahead of Thoma on 1,208 and Saturday's runner-up from Japan Kazuyoshi Funaki on 1,018.

Sunday's victory went to Japan's Akira Higashi, who defied difficult windy conditions in the north Slovenian resort and soared to 202 and 203 metres for his second World Cup win. He first topped the podium four years ago in Sapporo.

Norway's Lasse Ottesen was third with jumps of 198 and 183 metres. In Saturday's training, Ottesen broke his compatriot Espen Bredesen's 1994 world ski flying record of 209 metres -- also in Planica -- when he soared to 212 metres.
